situation: I've been feeling low for the last few months, and have been finding it hard to sleep at night.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: What brings you online today?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Can I help you with anything today?  We can just chat if you don’t have anything in particular you’d like to discuss.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I’m Kim.  What’s your name?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Hi there, I'd love some help

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Great! What’s going on?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I've been struggling with sleep over the last few months, and it's making me tired during the day.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I have been finding it hard to stay asleep, and wake up tossing and turning constantly.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Lack of sleep will definitely make you tired during the day!  Is there something bothering you that causes you to stay awake during the night?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I can't think of anything particular,  but my mood has been low generally for the last wee while which I imagine is probably the cause. I'm so tired during the day but as soon as my head hits the pillow at night I'm wide awake.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Well it sounds like you’re tired enough for sleep, but you’re still wired and can’t get the sleep you need.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's exactly it. Do you have any advice on what I can do?

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Are you getting any physical activity in during the day to make body more willing to cooperate?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'm working in a desk job so spend almost all day sitting down. That could be part of the problem.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: I’ve found that physical activity helps me to get to sleep even when I’m troubled mentally.  Another option is to slow your brain down so that your mind is relaxed.  That is much harder for me though!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That's a good idea. I could try go out for a walk either before or after work as a starting point and see if that makes a difference.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: That sounds like a good plan!  It also helps to make sure that it’s dark and very quiet.  Surprisingly enough, when they did research on sleep disorders they found that a lot of people just needed quiet and darkness.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Have you tried lavender? I have heard pillow or room sprays can be good for sleep.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Yep, I’ve tried a LOT of things.  I’m currently struggling with this myself.  I’m even trying out melatonin, tryptophan, and even CBD (not stoney weed oil)!  So far no success, but I’m still trying!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I've heard people mention melatonin - I might use that later if other methods dont work. It's good to know other people are in the same boat.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: It’s one of the reasons that it’s good to get outside.  Your body makes melatonin from sunshine, so going for a walk outside helps in 2 ways!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: If we had a little more sunshine where I live that would be fantastic!

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Getting good sleep is critical.  Supplementing with melatonin might help compensate for your lack of sunshine!

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: I'll look into it for sure. It's something I hadnt considered before this chat.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Glad I could help.

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: Thanks, the help was appreciated.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: Anytime.  Is there anything else you wanted to discuss?

dialog.speaker: seeker
dialog.content: That was all for today, thank you.

dialog.speaker: supporter
dialog.content: My pleasure!  Hope your day goes well.  Sweet dreams!
